content:
watchOS 27 will be coming soon as the next major software update for the Apple Watch. I've been testing the watchOS 27 beta this summer, and there are three new features I've especially enjoyed.

#1: A Brand-New Home Screen View

To be honest, Apple has never truly perfected the watchOS home screen. The original honeycomb design looked fine in promotional images, and the list view added later has been my go-to, but both options can feel clunky at times.

The issue is that the Apple Watch is designed for extremely brief micro-interactions. Plus, watchOS comes preloaded with tons of apps—not to mention third-party apps—so finding what you want amid a sea of ones you never use takes considerable time.

watchOS 27 offers a solution: a Smart Stack of apps, which has become the new default home screen view.

This Smart Stack is similar to a honeycomb-style grid view, but it only shows your five most frequently used apps along with the Siri app. Based on my experience, the stack has always contained the apps I want. On the rare occasions when it doesn't, you can still choose to open the full app view.

Most of the time, my watch face complications are my primary way of launching apps. Now, the Smart Stack serves as a handy secondary option.

#2: Tap Gesture

Over the past few years, Apple has gradually introduced various novel and interesting gestures for navigating watchOS.

Double Tap was the first gesture to debut, and last year Wrist Flick was added to the mix.

Now watchOS 27 brings a third option: Tap. It's similar to Double Tap, but it's a single tap and only works with the Smart Stack.

When browsing the Smart Stack, a tap with your index finger and thumb selects a marked widget. Essentially, it's a convenient selection tool.

You can now open the Smart Stack and navigate using Double Tap, then use the new Tap gesture to select a widget and launch the corresponding app.

#3: Siri AI

Siri AI is the centerpiece of Apple's new software lineup this fall, which also includes watchOS 27.

Apple has rebuilt Siri from the ground up for the AI era, making it a major upgrade over previous versions.

watchOS 27 adds a dedicated Siri app where you can browse your conversation history with the assistant across all your devices. Importantly, the Apple Watch's version of Siri is absolutely not some feature-stripped wrist edition—it's the exact same Siri AI you get on your iPhone, iPad, Mac, and other devices.

According to Apple's senior director of watchOS software engineering (as reported by TechRadar), this is one of the goals of this major Siri overhaul:

While several other companies are attempting to create successful AI wearables, the Apple Watch—already hugely popular—will become one of them, powered by watchOS 27.

Which feature of watchOS 27 is your favorite? Let us know in the comments.
